profile.headline: Senior Systems Software Engineer
profile.summary:
- Experienced computer engineer skilled at learning new fields and quickly becoming a technical expert
- Proficient debugger who searches specs and HDL and works with designers to find root cause and develop fixes
- Preferred contact for questions from other teams due to depth of knowledge and ability to convey concepts well

Skills
- C/C++/Assembly
- Baremetal driver development
- Pre- & post-silicon bring-up
- Software Porting
- Debugging with traces, waveforms, or Trace32 debugger
- Test development and optimization
- Python/Shell/Make scripting
- Code & Debug consulting
- New team member training & mentoring

positions.title: Senior Systems Software Engineer
positions.description: Skills: UEFI

positions.title: Senior Staff Engineer - Corporate R&D
positions.description:
Mobile AI SW on Accelerator chip (Jan 2022-June 2022)
- Architected a way to port a mobile AI inference backend to run on the AI Accelerator chip, using my Compute framework as scaffolding for the development
- Reviewed feature requirements and mapped them to existing features in the AI chip SW stack, and directed the coding changes required for the backend and the SW stack
- Developing and debugging new capabilities required for running the backend in the AI chip SW stack (including shared object loading and heap support)

positions.title: Staff Engineer - Corporate R&D
positions.description:
AI Accelerator Project

Compute framework (Sep 2021-Dec 2021)
- Took over development of a framework and compiler wrapper that allowed C & C++ code to be compiled to run on the AI Accelerator chip that was originally designed to only execute compiled ML models
- Brought the framework from not yet supporting single-core "Hello world" to being able to run multi-core examples

Platform Triage (Jan 2021-Aug 2021)
- Lead Platform triage, responsible for quickly analyzing new bug reports and routing them to the correct team
- Triaged and debugged issues throughout the SW stack including host side application code & user space driver code, as well as device side FW stack & user space code

Machine Learning Compiler (Dec 2019-Dec 2020)
- Became primary triage, debug, and inter-team support person for the ML compiler
- Assisted with bringup and debug of compiler-generated code on initial hardware
- Reviewed and rewrote error generation and reporting framework within the compiler codebase
- Developed a script to automate collection and parsing of debug information, providing a good first look at what went wrong
- Debugged tough issues including a multi-core synchronization race that blocked debug access to the cores, data corruption due to register corruption from interrupts, a stack overflow, and a hardware clock-gating bug

Baremetal Testcase framework (Sep 2019-Nov 2019)
- Developed a framework for converting baremetal tests to a format executable by the AI chip that provided support for OS-like functionality including TLB management, threading, logging, and memory management
- Demonstrated functionality for importing test cases from DV team, Mobile AI framework team, and MicroBenchmark framework team

Mobile AI inference framework SW (Jan 2019-Aug 2019)
- Ported and rewrote code and tests from C-based framework to new generation C++ based framework
- Enabled automated Jenkins regression testing, enhanced it to auto-trigger from git pushes and report status back to GitHub

positions.title: Staff Engineer - Post-Silicon Validation
positions.description:
Code Chief – Designed and wrote Validaton boot flow and baremetal bring-up/test OS for ARMv8-based server chips.
- First team member to boot chips to testcase start point in emulation and in bring-up labs, and first to start learning about and working on new chip revisions and designs
- Virtualized testcase framework to enable dynamic memory allocation, testcase concurrency, and complex VA != PA testing
- Created API for executing any portion of code at any desired security and exception level, to enable security testing
- Created full-featured MMU/SMMU API to create/modify pagetables for any desired test setup
- Rewrote interrupt (GIC) driver to enable runtime environment and testcases to independently register and unregister unique handlers for each interrupt, rather than being limited to a single, systemwide handler for all interrupts
- Trained new employees on boot and test environment, and became the team's go-to person for code questions and debug
- Performed code reviews of all shared code, often catching code bugs before they were pushed to git
- Handled software interviews for all prospective Validation team members (50+ interviews)

Unit Validation Lead – Lead the team responsible for emulation and post-silicon validation of integrated memories, integrated management controller processor, and security-related units.
- Wrote initial versions of testplans and tests using design specifications and verification testplans as reference
- Identified bugs and deficiencies in design documents, verification testplans, and unit logic
- Oversaw and reviewed the continued development of tests and testplans as members joined my team

(used C, ARMv8 assembly, emulators, on-chip debug facilities, Trace32 debugger)

positions.title: Staff Engineer
positions.description:
Pre-silicon Bring-up (Jan 2008 – Nov 2015)

Designed, wrote, and validated software & firmware reference code to bring-up, test, and debug POWER series chips and systems, working closely with the design teams and lab team to solve hardware and software bugs. Technical expert on code and processes, representing the team in design meetings, training and mentoring team members, and solving the hard problems.
- Debugged most of the bring-up code problems, particularly in the areas of the PLLs, clocking, scanning, and the logic involved in the initial power-on sequence
- Co-created a micro-controller emulator (US Patent 9134966), enabling test and debug of micro-controller assembly code two months before VHDL was ready and providing a 21x sim speed improvement vs. using the simulated micro-controller
- Optimized assembly code for a space-constrained environment, recovering 30% of max capacity
- Rewrote boot code to double its speed
- Discovered and tested the fix for at least one logic bug in each supposedly good chip design for four different chips
(used C/C++, assembly, simulators, traces, on-chip debug facilities, waveform viewers)

Post-silicon Bring-up (Jan – April 2009, Feb – Mar 2011, Jan – Mar 2013)

Debugged problems in the bring-up code, created and tested workarounds for problems found in the lab, and added new debug features to the code. Wrote and executed bring-up lab testplan for the L3 cache.
- Created L2 and L3 cache and directory logout code which was used to gather data for most lab bugs
- Developed a performance monitor to tune memory and fabric interconnect tests, resulting in tests that were an order of magnitude more stressful than the originals
- Discovered root cause and created fixes or workarounds for most problems within two days of initial report
- Drove adoption of an auto-compiled code repository, greatly reducing problems created by users running old code
(used C/C++, perl, traces, on-chip debug facilities and performance monitors)

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
Simulation Models (Aug 2007 – Aug 2012)

Created chip and system VHDL wrappers for three different POWER chip projects, built simulation models, provided scripts to load and initialize the models, performed initial regression and debug of errors, and trained users on the sim environment.
- Built and supported simulation models and scripts used by at least seven different teams (Virtual Bring-up, Power Management, Lab, Exercisers, DFT, Firmware, Performance) for code development and end-to-end testing, regularly making improvements based on user feedback
- Automated the process of creating and regressing models, reducing it from 8 hours to about 30 minutes of work
- Developed sim cheats that doubled performance when enabled
(used VHDL, perl, ksh)


Special Assignments (Nov – Dec 2007, Oct – Nov 2011, Jun 2012)

Assisted the memory controller logic design team (2007), pervasive verification team (2011),  and memory buffer chip scan verification team (2012) in meeting critical schedule milestones.
- Designed and semi-formally verified two memory controller logic blocks in time for milestone
- Identified and created a side fix for a common component to allow milestone to be met on schedule when an official fix couldn't be created in time by the logic owners.
- Started writing tests and filing bugs for pervasive logic after only one day of training, and succeeded in helping them meet their milestone

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
DFT

Generated manufacturing test patterns for a Cell BE derivative processor. Ran the automatic test generation tool, wrote manual tests to increase coverage, debugged test pattern problems on the tester, analyzed test coverage rates, documented processes and trained team members.
- Delivered manufacturing test patterns two weeks ahead of schedule and with improved coverage vs. previous chip
- Discovered a major bug in a third-party tool that reduced ATPG coverage by 15%, and developed a workaround that recovered all but 3% of that lost coverage, enabling manufacturing pattern delivery two months before the bug was fixed by the third-party.
- Developed a LBIST pattern analysis tool that showed current generation methods are near optimal for test time
- Certified to run the tester without supervision, becoming the first and only team member with that privilege
(used Cadence EncounterTest, Perl, Ocaml, Teradyne UltraFLEX tester)

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
OS/build environment porting

Ported a test OS and its build environment from an IBM environment (POWER/AIX/xlC/XCOFF) to a GNU environment (x86/Linux/gcc/ELF) in an effort to make it easy to release as open source. 
- Successfully created a functional build from scratch in three months working alone, whereas the previous two teams given this task failed to produce anything functional
- Documented the conversion process, issues, and resolutions, and reported numerous code bugs and bad practices
(used gmake, gcc, gas, binutils, sed, C, POWER assembly)

positions.title: Engineer
positions.description:
Sony/Toshiba/IBM Bringup Lab

Automated characterization of the memory and IO interfaces.
- Improved characterization test time from 2 minutes to 2 seconds
- Discovered a bug in third-party IP and verified the fix in the next revision
- Assisted Sony in setting up their own power measurement lab and found and fixed bugs in their scripts
(used C, Excel, Perl, ksh, Japanese)

positions.title: Co-Op Preprofessional Engineer
positions.description:
Sony/Toshiba/IBM Design Center

Model build automation.
- Automated model build process for a verification team in the first two weeks (was supposed to take all summer)
- Wrote and verified VHDL to speed up OS boot testing in sim, allowing early sim error detection
- Co-developed a common shell environment to allow script reuse across all IBM sites, which is still in use today
(used VHDL, ksh)

positions.title: Engineering Co-op
positions.description:
Device driver development.
- Developed device drivers for the mpc82xx processor family for a communications board
- Documented device driver API
(used C, VxWorks RTOS, MS Word)

positions.title: Electronics Engineer
positions.description:
Communications board characterization.
- Created guidelines and checklists for testing
- Characterized a communications board and documented results with waveforms
(used C, component datasheets, PCB schematics, digital oscilloscope)

positions.title: Technical Operations Specialist
positions.description:
Maintained about 200 Macs and PC across four computer labs, assisting students with academic and software questions and fixing problems.
- Successfully prototyped and completed automated rollout of Mac OS X across all four student labs
- Developed and presented staff trainings for software and hardware
(used AppleScript, Mac OS 9 & X, Windows 95)
